title: Week 21 Reading Quiz
description_html: Read both lessons before you start. Choose the best answer for each question. You may take this quiz twice, and your higher score counts.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.text_html: The 1st Texas lost more than 80 of every 100 men at Antietam in a single day. What can you infer about how Lee used the Texans?

answers.text: He gave them some of the hardest and most dangerous fighting.
He kept them in reserve far from the fighting and used them to guard supplies.
He used them only to guard the army's supply wagons.
He sent them home before the main fighting began.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.text_html: At the Wilderness the Texans shouted "Lee to the rear!" and refused to charge until he went back. What does this show?

answers.text: The soldiers trusted Lee and did not want to lose him.
The soldiers wanted to give up the fight and were trying to send Lee home.
The soldiers had stopped obeying every order.
Lee had little experience leading men in battle.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.text_html: John Bell Hood was a fine brigade leader but lost most of the Army of Tennessee in failed attacks. Which statement best fits the lesson?

answers.text: Hood was never brave enough to lead men into battle when under fire.
Hood refused to attack at Atlanta, Franklin, or Nashville and was relieved.
Hood's army was larger than any army that the Union had in the field.
Daring that works for a brigade can be dangerous in command of a whole army.

questions.name: Question 4
questions.text_html: Texas cotton was hauled to Brownsville and across the Río Grande to Matamoros. Why did this route work for the Confederacy?

answers.text: Matamoros was a Confederate port, and Texas troops guarded the whole of its harbor against the Union.
The Union army had built and guarded the road to the river crossing.
Mexico was neutral, so ships of other countries could dock there despite the blockade.
Texas ports had never shipped any cotton before the war began in 1861.

questions.name: Question 5
questions.text_html: Under the first plan for Reconstruction, Texas passed Black Codes in 1866. Why did Congress take over the plan?

answers.text: Black Texans had asked Congress to close the new schools and to send the army home again.
Congress and many Northerners saw the Black Codes as slavery under another name.
Texas had refused to hold any elections after the war.
President Johnson wanted the army to run every state government.

questions.name: Question 6
questions.text_html: Governor Davis asked President Grant to send soldiers in 1874, and Grant refused. Why would holding Davis in office by force have been hard?

answers.text: Davis had no enemies left among the people of the state of Texas.
Grant had no soldiers available anywhere in the whole country at the time.
The Freedmen's Bureau had asked Davis to step down from the governor's office.
Davis had lost by a wide margin, and many white Texans would have fought the army.

questions.name: Question 7
questions.text_html: According to the lesson, what did freedpeople do after the Union army announced freedom in Texas?

answers.text: Many searched for family and built churches and schools, though most received no land.
Most were given small farms by the Freedmen's Bureau and soon left cotton farming for good.
Nearly all stayed on the same farms under the same old terms.
Most left Texas at once and crossed the river into Mexico.
